intent_en: To illustrate the historical progression of human development in Asian nations, demonstrating how countries like South Korea, India, Thailand, and the Philippines have advanced from low to high development levels over time.
previous_intent: To illustrate the historical progression of human development in Asian countries, demonstrating the transition from least-developed to developing economies as seen in the rising indices of nations like South Korea, India, and Thailand.
narration_support: to graduate from the category of least -developed countries to the status of a developing economy. Other Asian countries like South Korea, India, Thailand or the Philippines have gone through a similar process often even faster.
chart_support: Line chart titled 'Historical Index of Human Development' showing an upward trend in development scores for South Korea, Thailand, Philippines, India, and Bangladesh from 1900 to roughly 2010.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly mentions the countries (South Korea, India, Thailand, Philippines) and the process of graduating from least-developed to developing status. The chart visualizes this as an increase in the Historical Index of Human Development for these specific countries (identified by flags) over the 20th and early 21st centuries.
